title: Shared drawers: Boss receipt
summary: The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
Two departments have exchanged lists of reading tags for their shared equipment shelf. Sol adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement sharedDrawersBossReceipt(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Set intersection. The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(n + d log d); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with set intersection. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

The input contains exactly two drawers. Produce the distinct readings present in both drawers, in increasing numeric order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.
